name: HubSpot Duplicate Cleanup and Lead Routing

parameters.content:
## 1. Start a run
Nightly schedule (only when SCHEDULE_ENABLED is true) or Run Now, a POST webhook that needs the X-Run-Secret header. Send {"dryRun": true} for a report without changes. DRY_RUN is on unless it is "false", and the Run Now body can never turn it off. Every setting is checked before any HubSpot call; Run Now gets a 500 that names each problem.

parameters.errorMessage: Run Now was called without the right X-Run-Secret header, so nothing was read or changed. If this was you, check RUN_NOW_SECRET.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ started: false, error: 'settings', problems: $('Run Settings').first().json.problems }) }}

parameters.errorMessage: ={{ 'Cleanup settings are not valid, so nothing was read or changed. ' + $('Run Settings').first().json.problems.join('. ') + '.' }}

parameters.content:
## 2. Read HubSpot
Owners, the property definitions the mapping tables are checked against, and every contact, 100 per page with the `after` cursor. Reads are tried 4 times, 5 seconds apart (a 429 waits out HubSpot's 10 second window). If a read still fails, nothing has been changed yet: the run stops with the reason.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ archived: false, dataSensitivity: 'non_sensitive', inputs: $('Run Settings').first().json.propertyNames.map(name => ({ name })) }) }}

parameters.errorMessage: ={{ 'HubSpot did not answer "' + $prevNode.name + '", so nothing was changed: ' + ($json.error && $json.error.message ? $json.error.message : 'unknown error') + '. Check HUBSPOT_TOKEN (a private app token with the scopes in the setup guide) and HubSpot\'s status page.' }}

parameters.content:
## 3. Find duplicates and plan
Exact matches: the same email (lower case, trimmed, Gmail dots and +tags ignored for EMAIL_DOT_PLUS_DOMAINS) or the same phone (digits only, with the country code) when the names agree and no two emails differ. Close matches: the same name plus the same company or email domain, or one phone with different emails or names. The record created first is kept. Exact matches merge automatically (up to MAX_MERGES_PER_RUN, never in a dry run); close matches only after a person approves. Right before merging, each record is read again and anything merged or deleted since is skipped.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ properties: ['email', 'firstname', 'lastname', 'hs_merged_object_ids'], propertiesWithHistory: [], inputs: [...new Set($('Plan Cleanup').first().json.merges.flatMap(m => [m.primaryId, m.secondaryId]))].map(id => ({ id })) }) }}

parameters.content:
## 4. Merge exact duplicates
One merge at a time with POST /crm/v3/objects/contacts/merge. HubSpot gives the merged record a new ID, so the next merge of the same group goes into that ID. 429, 423, 5xx and lost connections wait 2, 4, 8, then 16 seconds (BACKOFF_SECONDS doubles each time) and try again; a DAILY 429 is not retried. Every merge ends in Record Merge, so the report lists each one, also a group where a later merge failed. The merged records are then read again for the next step. That read also checks merges HubSpot answered with an error: if both IDs now lead to one record, the merge went through.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ properties: $('Run Settings').first().json.contactProperties, propertiesWithHistory: [], inputs: [...new Set($('Loop: Merges').all(0).flatMap(i => i.json.outcome === 'merged' ? [i.json.newId] : i.json.outcome === 'failed' ? [i.json.primaryNow, i.json.secondaryId] : []))].map(id => ({ id })) }) }}

parameters.content:
## 5. Fix fields and assign owners
Lead source and lifecycle stage values are mapped to the allowed set with LEAD_SOURCE_MAP and LIFECYCLE_MAP. Lifecycle stage only moves forward, as HubSpot requires. Unowned contacts get the next available owner from ROUND_ROBIN_OWNERS (AWAY_OWNERS are skipped); the rotation is remembered between runs. Records of one person share one owner. Only changed properties are sent, 100 contacts per batch update, with the same backoff as merges. If HubSpot refuses a whole batch because of one contact, its contacts are sent again one at a time.

## 6. Ask a person about close matches
One Slack message with an Approve and a Skip link per pair. Each link carries a token signed with APPROVAL_SECRET (HMAC SHA-256) that names the pair, the action, a one-time nonce and the expiry. The pairs are saved as waiting only after Slack accepted the message. Never in a dry run.

## 7. Report
One Slack summary per run: merged, waiting for approval, fields fixed, owners assigned, before and after counts and every problem. Any problem (a failed merge, update or Slack post, a bad owner in the list) ends the run as failed after the summary, so the error workflow raises an alert and nothing half done goes unreported.

parameters.errorMessage: ={{ 'HubSpot cleanup finished with ' + ($('Summary Not Posted').isExecuted ? $('Summary Not Posted').first().json.problems : $('Build Summary').first().json.problems).length + ' problem(s): ' + ($('Summary Not Posted').isExecuted ? $('Summary Not Posted').first().json.problems : $('Build Summary').first().json.problems).join(' | ') }}

parameters.content:
## 8. Approval links
Opening a link (GET) only shows a confirm page, so Slack previews and link scanners change nothing. The page's button sends a POST with the same token. Both check the signature (a forged link gets a 403 and an alert), the expiry (410) and that the pair still waits with this nonce (a used or replaced link gets a 409).

parameters.errorMessage: ={{ 'An approval link was refused because ' + $('Check Approval').first().json.reason + '. Nothing was changed. If nobody on the team changed a link by hand, someone may be guessing links.' }}

parameters.content:
## 9. Act on the decision
Skip: the pair is remembered and never suggested again. Approve: both records are read again; if someone already merged them or one was deleted, nothing is merged. Otherwise they are merged (tried 3 times) and the decision is saved, so the link cannot be used again. If the merge call fails, both records are read again: one record means it went through; otherwise the pair keeps waiting, the page says so and the run fails for the alert. Each decision is posted to Slack.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ properties: ['email', 'firstname', 'lastname', 'hs_merged_object_ids'], propertiesWithHistory: [], inputs: [{ id: String($json.payload.p) }, { id: String($json.payload.s) }] }) }}

parameters.errorMessage: ={{ 'The decision was saved, but its Slack note could not be posted: ' + ($json.error && $json.error.message ? $json.error.message : 'unknown error') + '. Check SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL.' }}
